chapter: Shows, scripts and the Mosby-era names
title: Eddie Rucker and Leon Hereford, the Army violinist
summary: Rucker was a Dreamland entertainer; Hereford, who served in the 25th Infantry band, accompanied singers on violin at the Dreamland and later played saxophone.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Oh, you also mentioned that Wood Wilson and his brother had a band. What was his brother's name? Do you know?
I haven't ever seen it written down any place. I'm just checking out these names in here. Johnnie Mac Venton. Ed Rucker.
Eddie Rucker. He was a entertainer in the night... in my nightclub.

Yeah, he was a violin player. He generally had a ...then he went, I think, with the Quality Serenaders and played saxophone. Yeah, he was in the Twenty-Fifth with us, and when he come...and when the Twenty-Fifth...when he got discharged, he come to Los Angeles, and I put

him in the Dreamland just to go 'long and play with the entertainers, see. The Black and Tan was up on the bandstand, and when the entertainers sing, he would go along and play the fiddle for...with the singers, you know. He was a good improviser. And then, after the Dreamland closed, they started the Quality Five, and he played saxophone in there, and then they went out to the...they used to call him "The Whispering Saxophonist." Oh, he would just whisper into the sax! And, anyway, when Sebastian's and everything opened up, he went out there, and he played out there quite awhile. Then something happened, and he got the band. And he didn't last long--two, three years he passed. He was a fine musician, though. He wasn't just like a jazz mus...'cause in the Army, he was the lead clarinet player, and you have to be up on your toes to play all that stuff 'cause we played in the Army--we played all that heavy stuff, you know. Yeah. All them big overtures and things that Army bands play. You know.
